Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB287.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zixianjue. Zixian Jue owns the retained deployment: three gates for whoever sits the curved-back chair — kill the founders leaving no trace, break the assembly's harmony unobstructed in every direction, and in the pile of sights and sounds walk, stand, sit, lie.

Senses.Explanation: Unobstructed in every direction: the freedom the masters grant only at the point where dodging is impossible — and the last word more than one of them died saying. Jieweizhou Xingzhou, after the great furnace has melted the six senses into one and the eighty-four thousand pores shed light together, has them shoulder the whole thing and walk straight into a thousand peaks — eyes through the four great seas, feet kicking the five Sumerus, unobstructed at the crossroads of the singing quarter, roaming at will through the flute-and-song crowds; Feiyin Tongrong closes his verse answer with the decree — neither color nor sound, pointing straight at what is ready-made: when the glance-thought returns home the dust-burden drops, and being unblocked in every direction is itself the whole true — and then raises the old case of the monk who asked the nun of Mushan what Mushan is; Yinyuan Longqi rules it of the senses themselves: seeing color unmazed, hearing sound unbeguiled, touched by things unturned, burdened by the body unburdened — roots and fields laid out clear and unobstructed, so that one may sketch the natural truth on Brush-tip Peak and play the flute sideways on the sleeping ox; Minshu Ruxiang, forbidding his heirs to beg grave inscriptions from officials, gives his last verse — I am the king of the teaching, free in the teaching; coming and going free, unobstructed in every direction — and passes sitting cross-legged. Zhulang Chesheng plays the extremes against each other — plucking beard-hairs before the hungry tiger's cheeks, snatching food from under the hawk's claws: sometimes holding shut, and no news at all; sometimes letting run, and unobstructed in every direction — so, is it holding-shut, or letting-run? No one judges, so he footnotes it himself; Konggu Daocheng lifts his staff: this truth belongs to none of the five phases and takes no yin and yang — originally round and bright, unobstructed in every direction; grasp it here and beings are buddhas, miss it and buddhas are beings — understand or not, thirty blows either way; Tianyin Yuanxiu, raising the old meeting of Dongshan Liangjie and Yunju Daoying — the one with no road to come by, whom Dongshan said no thousand or ten thousand could hold — rules it the meeting of working masters: a pearl rolling in the bowl, a bowl rolling on the pearl, unobstructed in every direction, nothing like the lost-headed shadow-chaser chipping ice for fire; Zixian Jue, taking the room, lays down the three gates for whoever sits the curved-back chair: first, kill the buddhas and the founders leaving no trace; second, break the harmony of the assembly, unobstructed in every direction; third, in the pile of sights and sounds, walk, stand, sit, lie — and plants his staff: who will build it with me?
